title: Overall program spec (charter) document structure
description: Canonical structure of an osuperpowers overall (program charter) document — charter only, zero implementation detail. The overall is the program's single source of truth: every mid-phase change returns here (backfill-as-version) before implementation continues. The four enforcement tables — Issue inventory, Phase inventory, Dependency graph, Change history — are the engine-side audit vocabulary (doc word = code word = engine token): rename a heading and you rename the validator with it. This schema is the single structure fact for the overall doc type: authoring agents read the properties below + their descriptions to draft conforming documents, docContractValidate consumes the same patterns (the enforcement position is the engine lifecycle, not a repo-local script). Section-numbered facets below are written under their literal `## ` heading (validator-keyed); the `Section N` numbers in the retired template were frame indices only.

header.description: Artifact header block — metadata at the top of the artifact, a bullet block, not a `##` section.

version.description: Current program version line (`- **Version**: vX.Y · YYYY-MM-DD`).

marker.description: The canonical `**Version**` marker — the engine derives its version-line assertion token (VERSION_HEADER_RE family, tokens.ts) from this const plus the line pattern.

line.description: Version line shape; the `v\d+\.\d+` token is the current version in the lineage (the file itself is the lineage source of truth — frozen docs legitimately pin the version in force at authoring time, fabricated / future tokens fail).

status.description: Status line — `- **Status**: Draft | Approved | In progress | Complete`.

author.description: Author line — `- **Author**: [human] · [harness + model at writing time]`.

form.description: Author is a free-text contributor line; pronouns and names carry no structural rule.

constraints.description: Constraints block — `- **Constraints**:` with project-level constraints, one per line; a strategy shift / lock-in decision is recorded here before implementation proceeds.

sectionHeadings.description: The four enforcement table headings — the literal validator-keyed vocabularies of the four-table audit (the '四表' of the closeout discipline).

issueInventory.description: Literal heading `## Issue inventory` (validator-keyed — the guard counts rows under this literal heading). Canonical even where an older artifact says `Requirement inventory`; do not copy the drift into new artifacts.

phaseInventory.description: Literal heading `## Phase inventory` — carries the canonical-form marker (`Implementation plan` column).

dependencyGraph.description: Literal heading `## Dependency graph`; a `(ASCII)` suffix is tolerated by the guard.

changeHistory.description: Literal heading `## Change history` (validator-keyed — versions strictly ascending `v<major>.<minor>`, no duplicates).

issueInventory.description: Section 4 — Issue inventory: every known issue / discovered requirement mapped to the phase that resolves it. Anchored forms (`#NNN#issuecomment-<digits>`) are machine-checkable; bare `#NNN` is ambiguous (AC numbers / PR numbers share `#`) and judged by hand. The table is the registration domain for anchors — an anchor referenced anywhere in the program must be registered here.

columns.description: Three content columns — `Phase | Issue (ref) | Title summary`.

row.description: Issue inventory row shape: `| P<n> | <issue ref> | one-line summary |`.

phaseId.description: Phase id token — the canonical `P<digits>(.digits)*` form (`P1`, `P2.1`, `P2.2.3`): `P` plus a digit run and dot-digit segments after it. Dotted digits mark sub-phase hierarchy — `P2.1` is the sub-phase of `P2`; the phase id is the registration unit of split/merge operations. Letter suffixes (`P2a`) and hyphens (`P2-1`) are not valid ids; ordering is the natural (major, segments…) order.

issueRef.description: Issue reference: anchored form `#NNN#issuecomment-<digits>` (canonical, machine-checkable) or the literal `none (dogfood session YYYY-MM-DD discovery)` for a none row.

titleSummary.description: One-line title summary — a single cell, no newline.

anchorForm.description: Anchored issue-reference syntax — the canonical machine-checkable form the registration domain counts.

phaseInventory.description: Section 5 — Phase inventory: the canonical 7-column table the four-table audit keys on — every phase row, its scope, its doc links, its acceptance condition and its dependency edge.

columnNames.description: The canonical 7-column header (7 column names, in this order).

count.description: Number of content columns — # Phase Scope Design spec Implementation plan Acceptance criteria Dependency.

header.const: | # | Phase | Scope | Design spec | Implementation plan | Acceptance criteria | Dependency |
header.description: The canonical 7-column header row (markdown draft form).

headerOpen.description: Header open token — `| # | Phase |` — the kernel the engine keys the Phase-inventory section on.

canonicalColumnToken.description: Canonical-form marker column — the engine's 'canonical file' test is the presence of this column name.

rowShape.description: Phase-inventory row shape (the row-shape guard — every `| P… |` row must carry the file-norm cell count; a merged/split cell shifts design/plan/dependency by a column and only detonates at closeout).

idFormat.description: Phase id token — the canonical `P<digits>(.digits)*` form (`P1`, `P2.1`, `P2.2.3`): `P` plus a digit run and dot-digit segments; dotted digits mark sub-phase hierarchy (`P2.1` is the sub-phase of `P2`), letter suffixes (`P2a`) and hyphens (`P2-1`) are invalid, ordering natural over (major, segments…). The identifier the dependency graph and the change-history claims reference.

cellCount.description: Split-cell count for one phase row — the 7 content columns plus the leading/trailing empties of the `|`-delineated row.

rowOpen.description: A Phase-inventory row opens with the leading pipe followed by the phase id.

cells.description: Per-column cell semantics (Scope / Design spec / Implementation plan / Acceptance criteria / Dependency).

pending.description: Unstarted placeholder value — `[Pending]` cell in the doc, `Pending`/`[Pending]` in backfill claims.

linkCell.description: A completed column carries a markdown link to the phase document (e.g. `[p1-design v1.1](2026-09-21-consumer-parity-p1-design.md)`).

done.description: Shipped completion marker for the plan cell — the backfill-claim ↔ column bidirectional check keys on it (`Pending` -> link; on ship, completion marker on the plan cell only).

dependency.description: Dependency cell cites the graph node with a hard (`->`) or soft (`-> (soft)`) edge — the edge token is a canonical phase id (`P<digits>(.digits)*`, e.g. `P2.1 ->`), the token the dependency-graph membership audit reads.

dependencyGraph.description: Section 6 — Dependency graph (ASCII): the phase dependency edges. Every `P<n>` token here must exist in the Phase inventory (membership audit) — add / split / reorder syncs the four tables together.

hardEdge.description: Hard-block edge: `P1 -> P2` — canonical phase ids (`P<digits>(.digits)*`) on both ends (e.g. `P2.1 -> P2.2`); the dependent must not start until the predecessor ships.

softEdge.description: Soft-suggestion edge: `P1 -> (soft) P5` — canonical phase ids (`P<digits>(.digits)*`) on both ends (e.g. `P2.1 -> (soft) P2.2`); non-blocking ordering convenience.

legendHard.description: Legend line defining the hard edge.

legendSoft.description: Legend line defining the soft edge.

changeHistory.description: Section 9 — Change history: append-only backfill record (version bump + date + summary + author per row). Every backfill claim lives here as a clause; the file itself is the version-lineage source.

columns.description: Four content columns — version / date / summary / author; the version token is `v<major>.<minor>`.

versionCell.description: Version cell token — `| v<major>.<minor> |` as the row's first content cell (the lineage cell the version tokens are checked against).

versionToken.description: Version token shape — `v<major>.<minor>`, strictly ascending and unique across the table (duplicates / out-of-order fail), date cell non-empty.

date.description: Date cell — ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, must be non-empty.

backfillClause.description: A change-history summary row may carry a backfill claim — a sentence whose keywords (`plan`/`计划`, `Design spec`) select which phase columns the `Pending -> <target>` clause backfills (the bidirectional backfill declaration ↔ column audit).

clauseSeparator.description: Claim-clause boundary — `；`/`;` split a change-history sentence into clauses; a claim only attaches the phases of its own clause.

claimPatterns.description: The CLAIM_RE family — the canonical claim pattern + the plan/design link words that select which columns a change-history claim backfills.

claimClause.description: Claim clause — `Pending`/`[Pending]` optionally followed by an arrow to a target token.

pattern.description: CLAIM_RE — the canonical single source: `(Pending|[Pending])` + optional `→`/`->` + a target that stops at whitespace / CJK punctuation / brackets so `→ **Done**（PR …` or `→ P4-design v1.0）` do not over-capture. An ASCII full stop is NOT a boundary — the canonical sub-phase grammar (`P2.1`, `P2.1-design`) embeds literal periods — so a trailing sentence period binds to the target and is normalized away by the claim-key stripper in the audit. Unanchored search (pattern-keyword semantics): the stop-set bounds the target token and trailing clause content (e.g. `（PR #1）`) is left unconsumed — the anchors must not be reintroduced.

target.description: Claim target — a `Done`-style completion token, or a `P<n>-design` token (a design-token target makes the clause a design claim), with trailing closing brackets stripped.

planLinkWord.description: Plan link word — a clause mentioning `plan`/`计划` carries a plan backfill claim (forward: claim ⇒ plan column non-Pending; reverse: shipped plan column ⇒ a matching claim exists).

designLinkWord.description: Design link word — a clause mentioning `Design spec` carries a design backfill claim (target must be a `P<n>-design` token).

designToken.description: Design-spec token — the canonical `P<digits>(.digits)*-design` token a Design spec column carries as its own completion marker and a design claim's target (`P2.1-design` registers under the sub-phase P2.1, never its base P2).

phaseReference.description: Phase references inside a claim clause — single or ranged (endpoints included).

single.description: Single phase reference — the canonical `P<digits>(.digits)*` form (`P1`, `P2.1`).

range.description: Ranged reference over canonical phase ids (`P<digits>(.digits)*`, e.g. `P1–P4` / `P2.1–P2.3` / `P1-P4` / `P1—P4`) joined by `-`/`–`/`—` — expanded to all phases including the endpoints.

programCharter.description: Section 3 — Program charter: goal (1–3 sentences), non-goals, cross-cutting constraints; acceptance criteria / API shapes / tasks excluded (charter only). Claims shrink, they do not inflate — what the program cannot prove it will not claim.

documentScope.description: Section 1 — Document scope: charter discipline — overall approval is not equivalent to any phase started (GATE); deviations update here first (backfill-as-version), then sync to overall.

filePaths.description: Section 2 — File paths table: one program date + feature slug under `docs/osuperpowers/` — overall `specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature>-overall.md`, phase spec `specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature>-<phase-id>-design.md`, phase plan `plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature>-<phase-id>.md` (lowercase phase ids).

boundaryRules.description: Section 7 — Boundary rules: each phase full brainstorm → plan → dev, shipped before dependents start; requirement changes discovered during a phase MUST feed back to this overall before implementation proceeds (version bump + change-history entry + sync affected phase acceptance/dependency).

maintenance.description: Section 8 — Maintenance: four tables backfilled per phase; charter only, no task lists — the phase spec carries the detail; strategy shifts / splits feed back immediately.
